It is recommended to formally request 125 external mutual assistance line contractor crews (approximately 500 FTE lineworkers) through the Regional Mutual Assistance Group (RMAG), supplemented by 20 vegetation management crews and 10 safety/damage assessment leads. input: What is the estimated cost-per-restored-customer for mutual assistance forces versus internal utility crew deployments?
expected_output:
### Executive Summary
**Mutual assistance forces exhibit an estimated fully loaded cost-per-restored-customer of approximately $485 to $650, compared to $140 to $185 for internal utility crew deployments—representing an average cost premium of 234% to 251%. This differential is primarily driven by portal-to-portal travel compensation, mandatory non-productive onboarding/safety briefings, staged lodging and per-diem logistics, and unfamiliarity with local circuit topologies.** While external Regional Mutual Assistance Group (RMAG) forces are cost-intensive, they remain essential for non-linear storm restoration velocity during Major Event Days (MEDs) to compress CAIDI and minimize regulatory outage duration penalties.

---

### Cost & Operational Comparison Breakdown

| Metric | Internal Crew Deployment | Mutual Assistance (RMAG) | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fully Loaded Cost / Restored Customer** | $145.00 / customer | $485.00 / customer | +234.5% | **Warning** |
| **Loaded Hourly Rate (incl. OT/benefits)** | $85.00 / crew-hr | $235.00 / crew-hr | +176.5% | **Warning** |
| **Staging, Lodging & Logistics** | $120.00 / crew-day | $650.00 / crew-day | +441.7% | **Critical** |
| **Productive Wrench Time Ratio** | 82.0% | 68.0% | -17.1% | **Warning** |
| **Restoration Velocity (Cust. Restored / Crew-Day)** | 38.5 cust / day | 22.4 cust / day | -41.8% | **Warning** |
| **Average Circuit Familiarization Delay** | 0.0 hrs (Baseline) | 2.5 hrs / feeder | N/A | **Warning** |

---

### Visualization Trigger

*Recommended Visualization:* **Grouped Horizontal Bar Chart** comparing cost drivers and operational productivity between internal and external mutual assistance units.

```json
{
  "chart_type": "bar",
  "title": "Cost and Productivity: Internal vs. Mutual Assistance Deployment",
  "categories": [
    "Loaded Hourly Rate ($/crew-hr)",
    "Logistics & Staging ($/crew-day)",
    "Productive Time Ratio (%)",
    "Restoration Rate (Cust/Crew-Day)",
    "Fully Loaded Cost per Restored Customer ($)"
  ],
  "series": [
    {
      "name": "Internal Utility Crews",
      "data": [85, 120, 82, 38.5, 145]
    },
    {
      "name": "Mutual Assistance Forces",
      "data": [235, 650, 68, 22.4, 485]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Actionable Recommendations

1. **Strategic Circuit Assignment (Topology Matching):** Deploy mutual assistance crews primarily on standard radial distribution feeders and lateral overhead lines with high customer density, reserving internal crews for complex networked circuits, substations, and automated FLISR-integrated corridors.
2. **Bird-Dog Pairing Ratio Optimization:** Assign one internal utility guide ("bird-dog") with direct SCADA/DMS visibility to every 2 to 3 mutual assistance crews to reduce circuit familiarization overhead and prevent switching errors.
3. **Dynamic Demobilization Thresholds:** Establish automated triggers within the Outage Management System (OMS) to release external crews systematically as feeder restoration curves plateau, transitioning tail-end, single-customer outages to internal daytime shifts to avoid exorbitant per-diem run rates.
4. **Regulatory Cost Recovery Tracking:** Ensure 100% of mutual assistance time-tracking, travel logs, and contractor invoices are mapped directly to FERC Account 593 (Maintenance of Overhead Lines) and flagged with storm-specific Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) codes for PUC cost-recovery prudence audits.

---

### Operational Safety & Tier 2 Notice

> **[TIER 2 ACTION REQUIRED - INFORMATIONAL / GOVERNANCE]**
> *Mutual assistance resource mobilization contracts and financial commitments exceeding authorized emergency thresholds require formal execution by Incident Command and Utility Finance executives. Mutual assistance crews cannot independently execute manual switching operations on physical grid assets without prior DMS/SCADA dispatch authorization from the System Control Center.*
